items.summary: The content-gap-analysis skill finds SEO and GEO content opportunities by comparing your site coverage against named competitors and scoring which gaps to close first. The skill contract expects a prioritized gap brief plus a handoff summary for memory/research, reading your domain, competitor domains, audience, goals, and any inventory while writing a user-facing analysis and reusable summary. Optional connectors include SEO tools, search console, analytics, and AI monitor, but the skill can proceed with user-provided URLs and content lists.

items.name: clean-code
items.author: wondelai
items.description: Systematically detect code smells and apply targeted refactorings that keep code readable and maintainable.
items.summary: clean-code applies a six-discipline framework for readable maintainable code during reviews, refactors, and new implementation. The core principle states code is read far more than written, so names, function boundaries, and formatting should optimize for the reader with a 10:1 read-to-write ratio cited in the docs. Six areas cover meaningful names that reveal intent without encodings, functions that do one thing at four to six lines with guard clauses and minimal arguments, comments that explain why not what with self-documenting code preferred, error handling via exceptions and null-object patterns instead of return codes, and unit tests following Arrange-Act-Assert with F.I.R.S.T. principles. A scoring rubric rates code 0-10 with specific gaps to reach 10/10. Triggers include code review, naming conventions, long functions, code smells, boy scout rule, and single responsibility. Cross-references point to refactoring-patterns for technique depth and clean-architecture for structural guidance. Applications span variables booleans functions classes constants collections with pattern tables and links to deeper reference files for naming, functions, comments, error handling, and tes.
highlights: Six disciplines: meaningful names, small functions, comments and formatting, error handling, unit testing, scoring rubri
Functions target one thing, four to six lines, guard clauses, and command-query separation.
Error handling favors exceptions, informative messages, and null-object patterns over return codes.
Unit tests use Arrange-Act-Assert, F.I.R.S.T. principles, and descriptive scenario-based names.

items.description: Quickly search 200+ icon libraries and retrieve production-ready SVGs without leaving the terminal or agent workflow.
items.summary: The better-icons skill Use when working with icons in any project. Provides CLI for searching 200+ icon libraries (Iconify) and retrieving SVGs. Commands: `better-icons search <query>` to find icons, `better-icons get <id>` to get SVG. Also available as MCP server for AI agents. Search and retrieve icons from 200+ libraries via Iconify. Before using any better-icons commands, ensure the tool is available in the environment. Option 1 Install globally (recommended, matches all examples below): ```bash Using npm npm install -g better-icons bash Using npm npm install -g better-icons Using Bun (faster) bun add -g better-icons Option 2 — Run without installing (prefix every command with npx or bunx): bash Using npx (npm) npx better-icons search arrow --limit 10 npx better-icons get lucide:home icon.svg Using bunx (Bun — faster) bunx better-icons search arrow --limit 10 bunx better-icons get lucide:home icon.svg
highlights: Search 200+ Iconify libraries and retrieve SVG icons via better-icons CLI or MCP tools.
